title: ETC European Tourism Trends and Prospects: Q3/2026
gist: Promotional page for a 21 October 2026 ETC/Tourism Economics webinar reviewing Europe's summer 2026 tourism season. It says the season was shaped by heatwaves, economic pressures and geopolitical uncertainty, and that the winter outlook will consider how energy costs could affect travel demand.

insights.claim: Oxford Economics says Europe's summer 2026 travel season was shaped by heatwaves, economic pressures and geopolitical uncertainty all at once.
insights.speaker: Oxford Economics
insights.so_what: Tourism-exposed European assets (airlines, hotels, southern destinations) faced overlapping climate, macro and geopolitical drags this summer.
insights.quote: Heatwaves, economic pressures, and geopolitical uncertainty all featured in this summer’s travel season.
insights.locator: Heatwaves, economic pressures, and geopolitical uncertainty

insights.claim: MMGY TCI Research is analysing how the summer 2026 heatwaves and droughts in Europe affected online sentiment and destination reputation, which treats climate extremes as a reputational risk for tourist destinations.
insights.speaker: Oxford Economics
insights.so_what: Climate extremes may push demand away from hot southern destinations toward cooler ones or toward shoulder seasons.
insights.quote: MMGY TCI Research will then examine how this summer’s heatwaves and droughts affected online sentiment and destination reputation.

insights.claim: Tourism Economics names energy costs as a possible drag on European travel demand in the 2026-27 winter season.
insights.speaker: Oxford Economics
insights.so_what: Higher energy prices could cut both household travel budgets and operator margins in European winter tourism.
insights.quote: Tourism Economics will close with an outlook for the winter season, including how energy costs could affect travel demand.

insights.claim: Related Oxford Economics events say higher-for-longer inflation will dent but not derail the Eurozone economy, and that Middle East disruption, supply constraints and El Niño are tilting commodity price risks higher.
insights.speaker: Oxford Economics
insights.so_what: The firm's house view combines sticky inflation with upside commodity risks, which supports its concern about energy costs for tourism.
insights.quote: Higher-for-longer inflation will dent, but not derail, the Eurozone economy
